thread:
maya: Heads-up — need to lock the sprint slate by EOD tomorrow. Acme cutover is customer-driven (they asked for a pinned fallback + migration window). We need acceptance criteria, bench plan, and a preflight checklist.
jon: got it. is this the customer that wants v1.2 pinned while we roll v2?
sasha: correct. Acme requires a pinned path for 30 days and a gradual traffic migration (10% -> 50% -> 100%) over 2 weeks. They also want bench numbers for latency + token cost before we flip.
maya: exact. product asks: define launch gates (perf + quality), regression thresholds, and rollback triggers. also confirm SLA impact.
leah: curious — do we have a compatible quantized variant for v2 to match cost targets? if not, we should avoid pinning to a variant we can't sustain.
jon: quick scan: v2-quant1 exists but latency is 12% higher at 1k seq vs v1.2-qt. Need a bench run with our real-world sample prompts from Acme (they sent a 5000-example set).
maya: Acme sample is in the shared drive: link: https://redwood.app/drive/acme-cutover-samples (internal). use their baseline prompts + our anonymized logs.
ram: ops-bot ran a preflight earlier today — pasted output below for context:
```
ops-bot: preflight report 3159876200
- capacity available: Dedicated pool D-3 (8xA100) -> 120 concurrent slots
- storage: KV cache warmup not yet measured
- infra flag: enable-gradual-shrink=true
```
leah: thanks. KV warmup is key — we should measure cold vs. warm latencies and include a suggested prefix-cache policy. I can run a quick cache-warm bench tomorrow morning.
sasha: acceptance criteria proposal (draft):
- perf: P95 generation latency <= 350ms for common prompt set at 16 batch size
- cost: per-token cost delta <= +15% vs v1.2 pinned baseline
- quality: n-gram BLEU-like metric + human spot-check regression rate < 3% (per eval set)
- rollout gates: initial 10% traffic for 48h with realtime quality alerting; escalate to 50% only if no alerts and cost within budget
- rollback: automatic fallback on >3% regression or P95 > 450ms for 2 consecutive hours
maya: nice. add a canary shutdown procedure (how to drain KV, rewarm, and rollback without customer-visible errors). also include comms doc for support.
jon: engineering asks: we need a compatibility shim for some function-calling schemas that changed in v2. can product quantify how many customers use those features vs how many will be affected?
maya: Acme uses function-calling for billing lookups heavily — they'll be in the affected cohort. we should mark this as high-risk and plan compensating shim or a soft-deprecation notice to them.
ram: ops-bot note: when we enable auto-fallback policy, routing will route to v1.2 pinned variant; please confirm the model-pin metadata key is populated in the catalog for customer tenancy.
leah: I'll add the model-pin metadata and a migration tag in the catalog. Suggest the pin TTL = 30d + auto-sunset option.
sasha: test plan items:
- bench matrix: cold vs warm, batch sizes [1,4,16], seq lengths [128,512,1024]
- evaluation: deterministic eval + sampled human review (50 samples per traffic cohort)
- failure tests: simulate KV cold-start, node OOM, and partial region outage with fallback enabled
- rollout choreography: canary -> monitor -> scale -> full flip -> postmortem
jon: timeline ask: can we get bench results + test runs by Tuesday AM so product can finalize SLAs for the customer?
maya: yes — target Tuesday 11:00am PT for bench artifacts and a one-pager with launch gates. If any blocker surfaces, flag in this thread.
leah: will run cache warmup bench tonight and post results here.
ram: ops-bot will schedule a canary window: Wed 03:00–07:00 UTC. tagging infra oncall.
ops-bot: @infra-oncall notified for canary window 3159950000.
sasha: one more ask — do we want to offer Acme a discounted migration credit if they accept a 7-day shortened pin? that might reduce tail risk.
maya: product is open to credits but need finance signoff. tagging @jon to loop finance.
jon: looping finance contacts now. also prepping a migration rollback runbook draft and will drop it here later today. :thumbsup:
leah: posting initial bench summary (short): P95 warm @ batch16 = 320ms, cold = 840ms, cost delta +9%. attaching CSV to the drive.
maya: this looks within gate. can someone draft the customer-facing migration timeline and the support escalation matrix?
sasha: i'll draft the migration timeline and the evaluation checklist. expecting a PR by tomorrow.
jon: putting rollback runbook link: https://redwood.app/runbooks/acme-migration-rollback (internal). includes steps to flip routing and invalidate cache gracefully.
maya: perfect. if we hit the proposed gates, product will greenlight the first canary. otherwise we push. thanks everyone — keep updates concise here so we can forward to customer ops. :handshake:
